decision_reason: Explicit negative-result documentation, not a finding: confirms the sunrise/gm deltaB mint is NOT flash-loan manipulable. Rejected as a non-vulnerability (recorded only to close the hypothesis).
disproof: To over-mint Beans in sunrise an attacker must inflate twaDeltaB within one block, but LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB reads ICumulativePump.readTwaReserves -- a season-length time-weighted average of cumulative reserves since the previous snapshot. A single-block flash-loan skew contributes negligibly to a season-length TWAP, and the minting oracle self-disables (deltaB=0) when twaReserves[beanIndex] < WELL_MINIMUM_BEAN_BALANCE or the USD oracle fails. The inverted-ternary getTokenPrice bug (BSA-001) is on the Chainlink source (not flash-manipulable) and the live BEAN:WETH/WSTETH wells price via LibEthUsdOracle/LibWstethUsdOracle, not the inverted branch, so it does not feed the live mint. Therefore no reachable single-tx path inflates the sunrise mint; the residual manipulable surface is the convert PENALTY spot path (FL-001), captured separately.
follow_up_packet: Negative result; mint path TWAP-defended. No action.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code (a defensive abs() helper, not a solvency/oracle/bridge/init guard). LibConvert.abs(int256.min) would revert on unary negation, but no reachable path produces int256.min: deltaB = calcReserveAtRatioSwap(reserves) - reserves[beanIndex] is bounded by realistic well reserve magnitudes far below 2^255. Theoretical-only, no fund loss. Rejected as Info.
follow_up_packet: Unreachable in practice; deltaB magnitudes far below int256.min. No action.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code (a reward computation, not a protocol-protection guard). LibSilo.stalkReward would only mis-behave if endStem < startStem, but every caller derives startStem from a stored deposit stem and endStem from the monotonically-increasing stemTip, and removeDepositFromAccount/grownStalkForDeposit require stem <= stemTip, so the invariant holds and the worst case is a checked-multiplication revert, not a wrong reward. Robustness gap only. Rejected as Info.
follow_up_packet: Invariant startStem<=endStem holds for all valid deposits; worst case is a checked revert. No action.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code (downcast notes). The two uint128 downcasts were re-derived: overflowing uint128 (~3.4e38) would require BDV magnitudes ~3.4e28 micro-BDV, orders of magnitude above any plausible Bean supply (~1e13 micro-Beans). Safe under realistic bounds; documented only for future-parameter caution. Rejected as Info.
follow_up_packet: Casts safe under realistic supply; no overflow path. No action.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code (token-pull accounting in a privileged-token path). LibFertilizer.addFertilizer credits the tokenAmountIn argument with a raw transferFrom and no balanceOf delta, which would drift only for a fee-on-transfer/rebasing Barn-Raise token. The Barn-Raise token is governance-controlled and currently wstETH (standard, non-FOT, reverts on failed transfer), so there is no live drift and the raw transferFrom cannot silently fail. Latent best-practice issue, no current impact. Rejected (Info-tier).
follow_up_packet: Live Barn-Raise token is wstETH (standard); drift requires a privileged FOT/rebasing token change. No present impact.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code. Documents the systemic 'records argument, not received amount' assumption across non-Silo token sinks, but every token through these paths is constrained to the governance-managed whitelist/unripe/Barn-Raise set (owner-or-Beanstalk gated), all currently standard non-FOT/non-rebasing tokens. The FOT/rebasing drain class is not reachable by an unprivileged attacker in this deployment. Rejected (Info, latent).
follow_up_packet: Requires a privileged whitelist change to introduce an FOT/rebasing token; not permissionlessly reachable. No present impact.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code. Fertilizer1155._beforeTokenTransfer calls payFertilizer (external Bean payout) using pre-transfer balances before the ERC1155 acceptance check -- an ordering/CEI concern. Fertilizer is owner-gated to Beanstalk whose facets are nonReentrant, and no fund-loss path was traced end-to-end from the token-integration angle. Cross-listed to reentrancy; no isolated exploit. Rejected (Info) pending no traced consumer.
follow_up_packet: No traced fund-loss path; settle-before-move ordering, Beanstalk facets nonReentrant. No action absent a traced reentry.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code (guard-consistency blemish). SiloFacet.safeTransferFrom/safeBatchTransferFrom omit nonReentrant relative to transferDeposit(s).
disproof: To exploit the missing nonReentrant an attacker must re-enter during the transfer, but both functions immediately route to transferDeposit, which IS nonReentrant and backed by the shared diamond reentrancy slot (s.sys.reentrantStatus); any reentry is caught by that inner guard. The functions perform no external token transfer or ERC1155 acceptance-hook callback of their own (deposits are internal accounting), so there is no callback window in which to reenter. The omission is cosmetic, not reachable.
follow_up_packet: Inner transferDeposit nonReentrant on shared slot defends; no external callback. No action.

decision_reason: Not safety-net code (guard-consistency blemish). ClaimFacet.mow/mowMultiple and ApprovalFacet.setApprovalForAll omit nonReentrant relative to siblings.
disproof: To exploit the missing nonReentrant an attacker needs an external callback observing inconsistent state, but mow/mowMultiple perform only internal stalk/seed accounting (LibSilo._mow) with no external call and no token outflow (asserted by the noNetFlow modifier), and setApprovalForAll writes a single approval-mapping slot with no external interaction. There is no reentry window, so the missing guard is unreachable. Cosmetic only.
follow_up_packet: No external call / no token outflow; noNetFlow asserts invariance. No action.
